narrative:
The model estimates a 48% chance that you will leave your current role, which is high enough for the organization to deny your promotion as a precaution.

The decision was driven primarily by three key aspects of your profile. Most influential was that you have received other job opportunities while at the company. Employees who stay rarely report such external offers, so this factor strongly pulled the prediction toward leaving. Second, your six-to-ten years of experience in your current organization worked in your favor; this tenure is longer than what most employees predicted to stay typically have, and it pushed the model toward expecting you to remain. Third, your overall career experience of six-to-ten years also nudged the prediction upward, as this level sits above the experience most stayers report.

Taken together, the pull from external opportunities outweighed the stabilizing effect of your tenure, tipping the balance toward a higher risk of departure.

The organization should discuss with you whether those outside offers remain active and explore ways to strengthen your sense of belonging. You may wish to reflect on what would make staying more attractive. Addressing these points openly could still change the outlook for future opportunities. (198 words)
